condition: drug resistant recurrent brief seizures despite dual anticonvulsant therapy
level_rationale: Continuing to experience 3 brief seizures each month despite taking 2 different daily anticonvulsant medications for 6 months meets criteria for drug-resistant seizures warranting outpatient neurology specialist evaluation, whereas having 3 brief seizures within the current hour constitutes an acute seizure cluster emergency requiring immediate ER care.

Continues to have 3 brief seizures each month

everyday_sources.source: Nwani PO, Nwosu MC, Enwereji KO, Asomugha AL, Arinzechi EO, Ogunniyi AO (2013). Epilepsy treatment gap: prevalence and associated factors in Southeast Nigeria. Acta Neurologica Scandinavica.
everyday_sources.title: Epilepsy treatment gap: prevalence and associated factors in Southeast Nigeria.
everyday_sources.evidence: Fifty percent of the overall treatment gap was caused by patients discontinuing AED treatment of their own volition despite continuing fits.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Nigerian and Indian English dialect lexicon swap ('brief seizures' vs 'brief fits', retained in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact seizure-rate window escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three atomic facts (age, 6 months of 2 different daily anticonvulsant medicines, and 3 brief seizures per month) with an exact 12-word vs 12-word span swap. Swapping only the rate window in atomic fact f3 from 'each month' to 'this hour' preserves identical digit tokens while shifting care from outpatient neurology specialist referral (level 3) to acute cluster-seizure emergency care (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
